summary: Al-Fatiha means 'The Opening.' It is the first surah of the Quran and a short prayer that Muslims say in every prayer. In it we praise Allah, say that He is the only One we worship and ask for help, and then ask Him to guide us on the straight path. It teaches us to start by thanking Allah and asking Him to show us the right way.
questions: Why do you think we ask Allah for guidance every single day?
What does it mean to you that Allah is the Lord of all the worlds?
What is one thing you can do this week to stay on the straight path?

summary: Al-Baqarah means 'The Cow.' It is the longest surah in the Quran. It explains who believers are and tells the story of Adam, the first human, who was given the job of taking care of the earth. It tells about Prophet Musa and the Children of Israel, including the story of the cow that gives the surah its name. It also teaches rules for daily life, like fasting, giving charity and being honest. It includes Ayat al-Kursi (verse 255), one of the greatest verses, and ends with a beautiful dua.
questions: What does it mean to take care of the earth the way Allah wants?
Which lesson or rule in this surah is hardest for you to follow, and why?
How does Ayat al-Kursi remind you that Allah is always watching over you?

summary: Aal-i-Imran means 'The Family of Imran.' It tells the stories of Maryam, her mother, Zakariya, and Prophet Isa. It teaches that Isa was a great prophet and a human servant of Allah. It also talks about the Battle of Uhud, where the Muslims were hurt because some did not follow the Prophet's orders. The lesson is to stay patient, stay united, and keep trusting Allah even after a hard time.
questions: What can we learn from the believers' mistake at Uhud?
Why is staying united so important for a community?
Think of a hard time in your life. How can patience and trust in Allah help you with it?

summary: An-Nisa means 'The Women.' It teaches about the rights of women, orphans and families. It explains how to share inheritance fairly, how to take care of orphans' money honestly, and how to be fair to everyone in the family. It tells believers to stand for justice, even if it is against themselves or their own family. It reminds us that Allah wants ease for us.
questions: Why do you think Allah gave so many rules about protecting orphans and the weak?
When is it hardest for you to be fair and honest?
How can you help someone in your family or community who has less than you?

summary: Al-Ma'idah means 'The Table Spread.' It begins by telling believers to keep their promises. It explains which foods are allowed, and it tells us to be fair even to people we do not like. It tells the story of two sons of Adam, where one killed his brother because of jealousy, which shows how serious it is to take a life. It also tells how the followers of Isa asked for a table of food to come down from the sky.
questions: Why is keeping a promise so important in Islam?
What can jealousy do to a person's heart?
How can you be fair to someone you do not get along with?

summary: Al-An'am means 'The Cattle.' It teaches that Allah alone is the Creator, and it points to the sky, plants and animals as signs. It tells how Prophet Ibrahim looked at a star, the moon and the sun, and understood that only the One who made them deserves worship. It also teaches us to be honest, to be fair when we weigh and measure things, and to be kind to orphans.
questions: Which sign of Allah in nature amazes you most?
What does the story of Ibrahim looking at the stars teach us about using our minds?
How can you be more honest in small things every day?

summary: Al-A'raf means 'The Heights.' It tells the stories of Adam and Iblis (Shaytan), and of the prophets Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut, Shu'ayb and Musa. Each prophet warned his people, and those who refused to listen were destroyed. It teaches that Shaytan is a clear enemy of humans, and that we should listen to the messengers of Allah and wear the clothing of taqwa, which means being mindful of Allah.
questions: Why did Iblis refuse to obey Allah, and what does that teach us about pride?
What does it mean to wear the clothing of taqwa?
Which prophet's story from this surah speaks to you most, and why?

summary: Al-Anfal means 'The Spoils of War.' It is mostly about the Battle of Badr, where a small group of believers won against a much bigger army with Allah's help. It teaches believers to trust Allah, to stay united, to obey the Prophet and not to argue with each other. It also explains that the things gained in war belong to Allah and His Messenger, so we should not fight over them.
questions: What does the victory at Badr teach us about trusting Allah when things look impossible?
Why is arguing with each other dangerous for a group of believers?
When have you felt Allah's help when you were weak or afraid?

summary: At-Tawbah means 'Repentance.' It is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah. It talks about treaties that were broken and about the hard journey to Tabuk in the heat. It describes the hypocrites, who pretended to believe, and the sincere believers who made mistakes but turned back to Allah and were forgiven. The lesson is to be honest with Allah and to repent sincerely.
questions: What is the difference between a hypocrite and a believer who makes a mistake?
What does sincere repentance look like in real life?
Is there something you need to ask Allah to forgive you for today?

summary: Yunus is named after Prophet Yunus (Jonah). The surah reminds us that his people believed in time and were saved from punishment. It also tells the story of Musa and Pharaoh, and how Pharaoh only said he believed when he was drowning, which was too late. It teaches that the Quran is a healing and a mercy, and that we should be happy about Allah's mercy.
questions: Why is it important to turn to Allah before it is too late?
What does it mean that the Quran is a healing for the heart?
How can you show that you are happy about Allah's mercy?

summary: Hud is named after Prophet Hud. It tells the stories of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb and Musa. Each people rejected their prophet and each was destroyed after the prophet was saved. Allah tells the Prophet Muhammad to stay firm on the right path and not to lean toward those who do wrong. The lesson is to be steady and patient when many people do not follow the truth.
questions: What helped the prophets stay steady when everyone rejected them?
How can you stay firm when people around you are doing wrong?
What does it mean to lean toward people who do wrong?

summary: Yusuf tells the whole story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). As a boy he saw a dream of eleven stars, the sun and the moon bowing to him. His jealous brothers threw him in a well, but he was taken to Egypt, was falsely accused, and was put in prison. Later he became the person in charge of Egypt's food stores. Many years later he forgave his brothers and was reunited with his father Yaqub. Allah calls it the best of stories.
questions: What did Yusuf do that shows great patience?
Why do you think Yusuf forgave his brothers instead of punishing them?
What does this story teach you about trusting Allah's plan?

summary: Ar-Ra'd means 'The Thunder.' It shows signs of Allah in nature, like thunder, lightning and rain, and says that even the thunder praises Allah. It has a famous verse saying that hearts find peace in remembering Allah. It compares truth and falsehood to foam that disappears and water that stays and helps people.
questions: When do you feel the most peace in your heart?
What does the example of foam and water teach us about truth?
How can you remember Allah more during your day?

summary: Ibrahim is named after Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). It includes his beautiful duas, like asking for a safe Makkah and for his children to keep up the prayer. It says that if we are grateful, Allah will give us more. It explains that prophets bring people from the darkness into the light, and it tells what Shaytan will say to his followers on the Day of Judgment.
questions: What is one blessing you have that you can thank Allah for right now?
What does Ibrahim's dua for his children teach us about caring for our family?
What does it mean to move from darkness into light?

summary: Al-Hijr means 'The Rocky Tract.' In it Allah promises to protect the Quran: 'We sent down the reminder and We will guard it.' It tells how Iblis refused to bow to Adam, how angels visited Ibrahim, and how Lut's people and the people of Hijr were destroyed. It tells the Prophet to be patient and to forgive in a beautiful way.
questions: What does it mean to you that Allah Himself protects the Quran?
What does forgiving in a beautiful way look like?
How can pride block a person from doing the right thing?

summary: An-Nahl means 'The Bee.' It lists many blessings of Allah: rain, plants, animals, the sea and the bee that makes honey. It teaches us to be thankful, to be fair and kind, to keep our promises and not to break our oaths. It also tells us to call people to Allah with wisdom and good words.
questions: Which blessing in this surah do you usually take for granted?
What can a tiny bee teach us about how Allah guides His creation?
How can you invite someone to goodness with kind words?

summary: Al-Isra means 'The Night Journey.' It begins with the night when Allah took the Prophet from Makkah to Jerusalem. The surah then gives rules for good character: be kind to your parents, do not waste, keep your promises, give full measure, and do not walk around proudly. It says the Quran guides to what is most right and straight.
questions: Why does Allah put kindness to parents right after worshipping Him?
What does it mean to be wasteful, and how can you be less wasteful?
Which of the rules for good character do you want to improve most?

summary: Al-Kahf means 'The Cave.' It has four stories that teach how to face four kinds of tests: tests of faith (the young men in the cave), tests of wealth (the owner of two gardens), tests of knowledge (Musa and Khidr), and tests of power (Dhul-Qarnayn). Muslims are encouraged to read it on Fridays. The lesson is to hold on to faith, to stay humble, and to remember that wealth, knowledge and power are all tests.
questions: Which of the four tests (faith, wealth, knowledge, power) is the biggest for you?
What did Musa learn from his journey with Khidr?
Why do you think this surah is recommended every Friday?

summary: Maryam is named after Maryam (Mary), the mother of Isa. It tells how Allah gave Zakariya a son, Yahya, when he was old, and how Maryam gave birth to Isa. As a baby, Isa spoke and said he was a servant of Allah. It also mentions Ibrahim, Musa and other prophets. The surah teaches that nothing is too hard for Allah, and that Allah is Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful.
questions: What does the story of Zakariya's dua teach us about never giving up asking Allah?
How did Maryam show trust in Allah during a very hard time?
What does it mean to you that nothing is too hard for Allah?

summary: Ta-Ha tells the story of Musa in detail: seeing a fire on the mountain, hearing Allah speak to him, his staff turning into a snake, and going to Pharaoh with his brother Harun. It tells about the magicians who believed when they saw the truth. It also tells how Shaytan tricked Adam. Allah says He did not send the Quran to make us miserable, but as a reminder.
questions: What dua did Musa make before going to Pharaoh, and why is it a good one for us?
What does it mean that the Quran is not a burden but a reminder?
How do the magicians show that the truth can change a heart quickly?

summary: Al-Anbiya means 'The Prophets.' It mentions many prophets, such as Ibrahim, Nuh, Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yunus and Zakariya, and shows how Allah helped each of them. It teaches that all the prophets were one community with one message: worship Allah alone. It also reminds people that the Day of Judgment is near while they are busy and forgetful.
questions: What do all the prophets have in common?
Which prophet's dua in this surah would you like to remember and use?
Why do people forget about the Day of Judgment, and how can we remember it?

summary: Al-Hajj means 'The Pilgrimage.' It tells how Ibrahim built the Kaaba and called people to Hajj. It describes how shaking and scary the Day of Judgment will be. It also gives believers who were treated unfairly permission to defend themselves. The surah ends by telling believers to bow, prostrate, worship their Lord and do good.
questions: Why do you think Hajj brings all Muslims together in the same place and clothes?
What does it mean to do good and to strive for Allah in the way He deserves?
How can you prepare your heart for the Day of Judgment?

summary: Al-Mu'minun means 'The Believers.' It begins with 'Successful indeed are the believers' and lists their qualities: they are humble in prayer, avoid useless talk, give zakat, guard their modesty, and keep their trusts and promises. It explains the stages of how a human is created, and tells the stories of Nuh and other prophets. It ends with a dua asking Allah for forgiveness and mercy.
questions: Which quality of the believers in the first verses do you want to build in yourself?
What does it mean to be humble in prayer?
How can you avoid useless talk and use your words well?

summary: An-Nur means 'The Light.' It teaches rules that protect families and society: modesty, lowering the gaze, and asking permission before entering a home. It tells how people spread a false rumor about Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and how Allah declared her innocent. It teaches us not to spread rumors. It has the famous verse of light, which says Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.
questions: Why is spreading rumors so harmful?
How can you protect the good name of other people?
What does it mean that Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth?

summary: Al-Furqan means 'The Criterion,' the thing that separates right from wrong. It says the Quran is that criterion. It tells how people mocked the Prophet. It ends by describing the servants of the Most Merciful: they walk humbly on the earth, answer ignorant people with peace, pray at night, are not wasteful, and ask Allah to make their families a joy to their eyes.
questions: How does the Quran help you tell right from wrong?
How can you answer someone who is rude to you with peace?
Which quality of the servants of the Most Merciful do you want most?

summary: Ash-Shu'ara means 'The Poets.' It tells the stories of Musa, Ibrahim, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb. After each story the surah repeats that in it is a sign, but most people did not believe, and that Allah is the Almighty, the Most Merciful. These stories comfort the Prophet Muhammad when his people rejected him and remind us that the truth wins in the end.
questions: Why do you think the same words are repeated after each story?
What do these stories teach about being patient when people reject the truth?
How does it help you to know that Allah is both Almighty and Most Merciful?

summary: An-Naml means 'The Ant.' It tells how Prophet Sulayman could understand animals. An ant warned its friends to go inside, and Sulayman smiled and thanked Allah. It tells of the hoopoe bird who told Sulayman about the Queen of Saba, who worshipped the sun and later believed in Allah. The surah teaches thankfulness, humility, and that all power really belongs to Allah.
questions: What did Sulayman do when he was given great power and blessings?
What can the ant teach us about caring for others?
How can you show thankfulness for the abilities Allah gave you?

summary: Al-Qasas means 'The Stories.' It tells Musa's story from his birth: his mother put him in the river, he grew up in Pharaoh's palace, he left Egypt after a mistake, and he became a prophet in Madyan. It also tells about Qarun, a man who became very rich and proud, and whom the earth swallowed. The lessons are that Allah protects those who trust Him and that pride leads to ruin.
questions: How did Allah take care of Musa when he was a baby?
What mistake did Qarun make with his wealth?
How can you stay humble when Allah gives you something good?

summary: Al-Ankabut means 'The Spider.' It says believers will be tested so that true faith can be seen. It tells how Nuh called his people for 950 years, and mentions Ibrahim and Lut. It compares people who depend on anyone other than Allah to a spider's house, which is the weakest of houses. The lesson is to be patient in hard tests and to depend on Allah.
questions: Why does Allah test people who believe?
What does the spider's house teach about depending on things other than Allah?
What is a test you are going through right now, and how can you meet it with patience?

summary: Ar-Rum means 'The Romans.' It begins by telling that the Romans, who had just lost a war, would win within a few years, and this came true. It lists signs of Allah: how humans were made from dust, how spouses bring love and calm, different languages and colors, sleep, and lightning and rain. It tells us to stay firm and keep our promise to Allah.
questions: Which sign of Allah in this surah makes you think the most?
What does it mean that Allah put love and mercy between spouses?
How does the story of the Romans show that Allah's promise is true?

summary: Luqman is named after Luqman, a wise man. The surah gives his advice to his son: do not put anyone beside Allah, be good to your parents, even a deed as small as a mustard seed will be brought forth, pray, tell people to do good, be patient, do not be proud, and lower your voice. It is like a short guide to wisdom and good manners.
questions: Which piece of Luqman's advice is the most useful for you today?
What does it mean that even a mustard seed's weight of a deed will be brought?
Why do you think Luqman told his son to lower his voice?

summary: As-Sajdah means 'The Prostration.' It talks about how Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days and made humans from clay. It describes believers who leave their beds at night to pray, hoping for Allah's mercy and fearing His punishment. It says that no one knows what joy is hidden for them in Paradise. It is reported that the Prophet used to recite it in the Friday dawn prayer.
questions: Why do you think waking at night to pray is so special?
What do you think is the joy that is hidden for believers?
How can you build the habit of making dua at night?

summary: Al-Ahzab means 'The Combined Forces.' It tells about the Battle of the Trench, when many tribes joined together to attack Madinah. The Muslims dug a trench, stayed patient and trusted Allah, and Allah sent a wind that scattered the enemy. It says the Prophet is an excellent example to follow. It also gives rules about the Prophet's family and about modesty.
questions: What helped the believers stay strong during the Battle of the Trench?
In what ways is the Prophet an excellent example for you?
How can you trust Allah when you are afraid?

summary: Saba means 'Sheba.' It tells about Prophets Dawud and Sulayman, who were given great gifts, and how Sulayman was given control over the wind and the jinn. It tells about the people of Saba, who lived in beautiful gardens but were ungrateful, so Allah sent a flood that destroyed their dam. The lesson is to be thankful for the blessings you have.
questions: What blessings did the people of Saba lose, and why?
How do you show that you are grateful, and not only say it?
What gift or ability has Allah given you that you can use to help others?

summary: Fatir means 'The Originator.' It says Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and that He made angels messengers with wings. It points to rain, mountains and the different colors of people and animals as signs. It says that those who truly fear Allah are the ones who have knowledge. It warns that Shaytan is an enemy and that no one will carry another person's burden.
questions: Why do you think knowledge makes people fear Allah more?
What does it mean that no one carries another person's burden?
How can you treat Shaytan as your enemy in daily life?

summary: Ya-Sin is often called the heart of the Quran. It tells about a town to which messengers were sent, and a man who came running from the far side of the city to tell people to follow them. It shows signs of Allah, like dead land coming back to life, the night and the day, and the sun and the moon each moving in its own path. It speaks about the Day of Judgment and says that when Allah wants something, He only says 'Be' and it is.
questions: Why did the man run from the far end of the city to give advice?
Which sign of Allah in this surah is the most amazing to you?
What does it mean to you that Allah only says 'Be' and it is?

summary: As-Saffat means 'Those Who Stand in Rows.' It begins with angels standing in rows. It tells how Ibrahim broke the idols and how he was ready to sacrifice his son, until Allah replaced it with a great sacrifice. It also tells of Nuh, Musa and Harun, Ilyas, Lut and Yunus. It ends with 'Glory to your Lord, the Lord of honor, and peace be upon the messengers.'
questions: What does the story of Ibrahim and his son teach about obeying Allah?
How did Yunus show he was sincere when he was inside the whale?
What does it mean to submit completely to Allah?

summary: Sad is a surah that mentions Prophets Dawud, Sulayman and Ayyub (Job). Ayyub became very sick and lost much, but stayed patient, and Allah healed him. It also tells how Iblis refused to bow to Adam because of pride. The surah teaches patience in hard times, turning back to Allah after mistakes, and avoiding pride.
questions: What can you learn from Ayyub's patience when he was sick and had lost so much?
How did pride cause Iblis to be thrown out?
When you make a mistake, how do you turn back to Allah?

summary: Az-Zumar means 'The Groups.' It tells us to worship Allah sincerely, with pure devotion. It has the famous verse: 'Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed Allah forgives all sins.' It describes how, on the Day of Judgment, people will be led in groups to either the Fire or to Paradise.
questions: What does it mean to worship Allah sincerely?
Why is it wrong to lose hope in Allah's mercy, even after big mistakes?
What would you say to a friend who feels Allah cannot forgive them?

summary: Ghafir means 'The Forgiver.' It shows that Allah forgives sins and accepts repentance. It tells about a believing man from Pharaoh's family who hid his faith and then spoke up for Musa. It tells that the angels who carry the Throne ask forgiveness for the believers. In it, Allah says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'
questions: What does it mean to you that Allah says 'Call upon Me; I will respond'?
What gave the believing man from Pharaoh's family the courage to speak?
How can you make dua more often?

summary: Fussilat means 'Explained in Detail.' It says the Quran was made clear in Arabic for people who know. It tells about the people of Ad and Thamud, and says that on the Day of Judgment people's ears, eyes and skins will speak about what they did. It has a beautiful verse about answering bad behavior with good behavior, so that an enemy can become like a close friend.
questions: Think of a time someone was rude to you. How could you answer with something good?
What does it mean that our own body parts will speak on the Day of Judgment?
Why is it hard to respond to bad with good, and how can you practice it?

summary: Ash-Shura means 'Consultation.' It describes believers as people who settle their matters by talking and consulting together. It says all prophets were given one message. It praises forgiving: whoever pardons and makes peace, their reward is with Allah. It says Allah speaks to humans by revelation, from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger.
questions: Why is it good to ask others for advice before making a decision?
What does forgiveness do for your own heart?
How can you make peace in a situation where people are upset with each other?

summary: Az-Zukhruf means 'Gold Ornaments.' Some people thought a person's worth was based on gold and wealth. Allah says the life of this world is only a small enjoyment, and the next life is for those who are mindful of Him. It mentions Ibrahim leaving idol worship and Isa as a sign. It says close friends on that Day will become enemies, except those who were mindful of Allah.
questions: Does having more things make a person better? Why or why not?
What makes a friendship last into the next life?
How can you remember that this world is only a short stop?

summary: Ad-Dukhan means 'The Smoke.' It says the Quran was sent down on a blessed night. It reminds us of Pharaoh's people, who left behind gardens and springs and fine homes, and had to leave it all. It warns about the Day of Judgment and promises gardens and safety to those who were mindful of Allah.
questions: What did Pharaoh's people have to leave behind, and what does that tell us about possessions?
What is the blessed night that the Quran was sent down?
What will you want to have brought with you to the next life?

summary: Al-Jathiyah means 'The Kneeling.' It points to signs in the heavens and the earth, the night and day, rain and wind. It says not to make your own desires your god. It tells that on the Day of Judgment every nation will be kneeling, and each will be called to its record of deeds.
questions: What does it mean to make your own desires your god?
Which sign of Allah in nature do you see most often?
How can you tell if you are following Allah's guidance or just your own desires?

summary: Al-Ahqaf means 'The Wind-Curved Sandhills.' It tells about the people of Ad, who lived among sand dunes and were destroyed by a strong wind. It tells us to be kind to our parents, and it has the dua of a person who reaches forty years old and asks Allah to help him be thankful. It also tells how a group of jinn listened to the Quran and went back to warn their people.
questions: Why does Allah mention parents so often in the Quran?
What would you ask Allah to help you with when you reach forty?
What can we learn from the jinn who listened and then spread the message?

summary: Surah Muhammad teaches how believers should act in times of conflict and tells them to obey Allah and His Messenger. It says that if believers help Allah's cause, He will help them and make their feet firm. It asks, 'Do they not think deeply about the Quran, or are there locks on their hearts?' It says Allah is the Rich and we are the ones in need.
questions: What does it mean to help Allah's cause in your daily life?
What can you do to think deeply about the Quran?
How does it feel to know that Allah is Rich and you are in need?

summary: Al-Fath means 'The Victory.' It was revealed after the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, which looked like a loss but turned out to be a clear victory. It tells how the believers promised loyalty to the Prophet under a tree, and Allah put calm (sakinah) in their hearts. It describes the Prophet's companions as strong against disbelief, merciful among themselves, and always bowing and prostrating.
questions: Why did the treaty look like a loss but turn out to be a victory?
What does it mean to have calm in your heart?
What qualities of the companions would you like to have?

summary: Al-Hujurat means 'The Rooms.' It is a surah about good manners: lower your voice around the Prophet, check the news before believing it, make peace between people who fight, and do not mock others, call them bad names, spy on them or talk behind their backs. Verse 13 says that people were made into different nations and tribes so they may know each other, and the best is the one who is most mindful of Allah.
questions: Why should we check news before sharing or believing it?
What is the worst thing about backbiting?
What does it mean that the best person is the one who is most mindful of Allah?

summary: Qaf begins with the letter Qaf. It talks about the resurrection and Allah's power to bring people back to life. It says that Allah is closer to us than our jugular vein, and that two angels write down every word we say. It says that every soul will come with someone driving it and someone to witness. It uses dead land coming alive after rain as a sign.
questions: How does it feel to know that two angels write down what you say?
What does it mean that Allah is closer than your jugular vein?
What word do you want to say more often, knowing it is being written?

summary: Adh-Dhariyat means 'The Winds That Scatter.' It begins with oaths by the winds and then talks about signs of Allah. It tells the story of Ibrahim's guests, who gave him the happy news of a son. It mentions the people of Lut, Pharaoh, Ad, Thamud and Nuh. It has the famous verse: 'I did not create jinn and humans except to worship Me.'
questions: What does it mean to worship Allah in daily life, not only in prayer?
How did Ibrahim show good manners to his guests?
What is something you do that you can turn into an act of worship?

summary: At-Tur means 'The Mount.' It begins with an oath by Mount Sinai, where Musa spoke with Allah. It says the Day of Judgment is certain, and describes how people of Paradise will enjoy time with their families. It tells the Prophet to be patient with the decision of his Lord and to glorify Allah when he gets up and at night.
questions: What does it mean to be patient with the decision of your Lord?
When do you usually find time to glorify Allah?
How can your family be together in Paradise?

summary: An-Najm means 'The Star.' It describes how the Prophet saw Jibril and went up to the Lote Tree of the Furthest Boundary. It says he does not speak from his own desire. It says idols are only names people made up. It says no one will carry another person's burden, and that a person only gets what he works for. It ends with the command to prostrate.
questions: What does it mean that a person only gets what he strives for?
Why are idols just names?
How can you prostrate to Allah with a humble heart today?

summary: Al-Qamar means 'The Moon.' It begins with the moon splitting as a sign, but people called it magic. It tells of the people of Nuh, Ad, Thamud, Lut and Pharaoh, and what happened to them. It repeats: 'We have made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?'
questions: What does it mean that the Quran is made easy to remember?
Why do people refuse to believe even when they see signs?
What can you do this week to learn a little more of the Quran?

summary: Ar-Rahman means 'The Most Merciful.' It begins with Allah's name Ar-Rahman and lists His gifts: He taught the Quran, created humans, taught speech, and set the sun and the moon in their paths. It repeats the question 'So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?' many times. It describes two gardens for those who fear standing before their Lord.
questions: Which of Allah's favors in this surah do you notice most?
Why does Allah repeat the same question so many times?
What favor of Allah have you forgotten to thank Him for?

summary: Al-Waqi'ah means 'The Inevitable Event.' It describes the Day of Judgment, when people will be in three groups: the foremost, who are nearest to Allah; the companions of the right; and the companions of the left. It describes Paradise and Hell, and points to signs like the seed you plant, the water you drink and the fire you light. It says the Quran is a noble recitation.
questions: Which group would you like to be with, and what can you do to get there?
What does it mean that the seed you plant is really grown by Allah?
What does it mean to you that the Quran is noble?

summary: Al-Hadid means 'The Iron.' It says everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah. It tells us to spend in His way and says the life of this world is only play and show. It tells us to race to forgiveness. It says Allah sent down iron, which has great strength and many benefits. It reminds us that Allah is with us wherever we are.
questions: What does it mean that the life of this world is play and show?
How can you spend in Allah's way even if you have little?
How does it change your actions to know that Allah is with you wherever you are?

summary: Al-Mujadila means 'The Woman Who Pleaded.' It begins with a woman named Khawla who came to the Prophet to complain about her husband, and Allah heard her and sent down verses. It teaches manners: make room for others in a gathering, and do not hold secret talks that cause harm. It says true believers do not make close friends with those who oppose Allah.
questions: What does it mean that Allah hears even the quietest complaint?
How can you make room for others in your classroom, workplace, or home?
Why are secret whispers harmful to a group?

summary: Al-Hashr means 'The Gathering.' It tells how the tribe of Banu Nadir was sent out of Madinah after breaking their agreement. It praises the Ansar, the helpers of Madinah, who gave others preference over themselves even though they were in need. It says that if this Quran had come down on a mountain, it would crumble from fear of Allah. It ends with many of Allah's beautiful names.
questions: What does it mean to prefer others over yourself?
How would you feel if the mountain would crumble from the Quran, but your heart stays hard?
Which of Allah's beautiful names at the end speaks to you most?

summary: Al-Mumtahanah means 'The Woman Who Is Examined.' It tells believers not to take as close friends those who fight against their faith. But Allah does not forbid being kind and fair to those who did not fight you. It gives Ibrahim as an example of someone who stayed firm. It also gives rules for believing women who migrated.
questions: How can you be kind and fair to people who believe differently from you?
What does it mean to stay firm like Ibrahim?
Why is justice important even toward people you disagree with?

summary: As-Saff means 'The Ranks.' It begins by asking, 'Why do you say what you do not do?' It says Allah loves those who stand together in rows like a solid building. It says that Isa gave good news of a messenger coming after him whose name is Ahmad. It tells believers to be helpers of Allah, like the disciples of Isa.
questions: Are there things you say you will do but don't? How can you change that?
What does it mean to be like a solid building together with other believers?
How can you be a helper of Allah today?

summary: Al-Jumu'ah means 'Friday.' It tells believers that when they hear the call for Friday prayer, they should hurry to the remembrance of Allah and leave their business, and after the prayer they can spread out and look for Allah's bounty. It gives the example of people who were given the Torah but did not act on it, like a donkey carrying books.
questions: Why do you think Allah tells us to leave our business for Friday prayer?
What does it mean to carry knowledge but not act on it?
How can you make your Fridays more special?

summary: Al-Munafiqun means 'The Hypocrites.' It describes people who say they believe but do not believe in their hearts. They look nice and speak well, but they are like wood propped against a wall. It says, 'Do not let your wealth or your children distract you from remembering Allah,' and tells us to spend in charity before death comes.
questions: How can you tell if your words and heart match?
What are things that distract you most from remembering Allah?
What good deed would you like to do before it is too late?

summary: At-Taghabun means 'Mutual Loss and Gain.' It says everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah. It reminds us that our spouses and children can be a test, and tells us to be mindful of Allah as much as we can. It tells us to listen, obey and spend in charity, because whoever is protected from his own greed is successful.
questions: How can family be a test as well as a blessing?
What does it mean to be protected from your own greed?
What does 'as much as you can' teach you about how Allah treats us?

summary: At-Talaq means 'Divorce.' It gives rules for how divorce should be done fairly, with a waiting period, without harming anyone, and with fear of Allah. It says, 'Whoever fears Allah, He will make a way out for him and provide for him from where he does not expect.'
questions: Why does Allah want us to be fair even in hard times like divorce?
What does it mean that Allah will make a way out for the one who fears Him?
When has Allah provided for you in a way you did not expect?

summary: At-Tahrim means 'Prohibition.' It begins with matters in the Prophet's home and teaches honesty and care within the family. It tells believers to turn to Allah with sincere repentance. It gives examples of women of faith, like Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and Maryam, to show that a person's faith is their own and that nobody's closeness to a wrongdoer can harm them if they believe.
questions: What does sincere repentance look like?
What can you learn from Asiya, who stayed faithful in Pharaoh's palace?
How can you protect yourself and your family from harm?

summary: Al-Mulk means 'The Sovereignty.' It says that all dominion belongs to Allah, who created death and life to test who is best in deeds. It asks us to look at the sky and see that there is no flaw in it, and to look at the birds spreading their wings. It asks, 'Who is there to provide for you if Allah withholds His provision?' Many Muslims recite it at night.
questions: What does it mean that life and death are a test of who does best in deeds?
What flawless thing in creation makes you think of Allah?
How can you remember that all your provision comes from Allah?

summary: Al-Qalam means 'The Pen.' It begins with an oath by the pen and says the Prophet has a great character. It tells the story of the owners of a garden who planned to harvest without saying 'if Allah wills,' and lost everything. It reminds the Prophet to be patient and not to be like the companion of the fish, Yunus, when he was upset.
questions: Why is it important to say 'if Allah wills' when we make plans?
What makes a person's character great?
What does the story of the garden owners teach about greed?

summary: Al-Haqqah means 'The Inevitable Reality.' It describes the Day of Judgment and tells what happened to Thamud, Ad and Pharaoh. It describes people who will be given their record in the right hand and say joyfully, 'Here, read my record!' and others who will be given it in the left hand and regret. It says the Quran is the word of a noble messenger and the certain truth.
questions: How do you feel when you imagine receiving your record on that Day?
What can you do each day to fill your record with good?
Why does Allah remind us of the nations that were destroyed?

summary: Al-Ma'arij means 'The Ascending Stairways.' It says that humans are created hasty and anxious: they complain when they are touched by bad, and are stingy when they have good. But not those who pray regularly, give to those in need, believe in the Day of Judgment, guard their modesty and keep their trusts. It tells the Prophet to be patient with a beautiful patience.
questions: When do you feel the most anxious, and what can you do about it?
Which quality of those who are saved do you want most?
What does a 'beautiful patience' look like?

summary: Nuh is named after Prophet Nuh (Noah). It tells how he called his people night and day, in secret and in public, asking them to ask forgiveness so that Allah would send rain and give them wealth and children. They put their fingers in their ears. After a very long time, they were destroyed by the flood. It ends with Nuh's dua asking Allah to forgive him, his parents and the believers.
questions: What can we learn from Nuh's patience over such a long time?
What does asking forgiveness bring according to this surah?
What dua would you like to make for your parents and family?

summary: Al-Jinn is about a group of jinn who listened to the Quran and said, 'We have heard a wonderful recitation that guides to what is right, and we believed.' It teaches that the jinn and humans are both in Allah's hands, that only Allah knows the unseen, and that the mosques belong to Allah, so no one should call on anyone else with Him.
questions: What did the jinn notice about the Quran when they first heard it?
What does it mean that only Allah knows the unseen?
How can you show respect for the mosque?

summary: Al-Muzzammil means 'The One Wrapped in Garments.' Allah tells the Prophet to stand in prayer for part of the night and to recite the Quran slowly and clearly. It says the night is a time when the heart is most focused. It tells him to be patient and to take Allah as his guardian, and to pray, give zakat and ask for forgiveness.
questions: Why is reciting the Quran slowly and clearly important?
What is a quiet time in your day when you can focus on Allah?
What does it mean to take Allah as your guardian?

summary: Al-Muddaththir means 'The One Wrapped in a Cloak.' It is among the early surahs. Allah tells the Prophet to get up and warn people, to say that his Lord is great, to keep his clothes clean, to stay away from what is wrong, not to give hoping to get more, and to be patient for his Lord. It says every soul is held for what it earned.
questions: What does it mean to keep yourself clean inside and out?
Why should we give without expecting something back?
What is something you can be patient about for Allah's sake?

summary: Al-Qiyamah means 'The Resurrection.' Allah swears by the Day of Resurrection and by the soul that blames itself. It asks if people think He cannot put their bones back together, when He can even remake their fingertips. It describes faces that are bright and looking at their Lord, and faces that are gloomy. It says man will not be left without purpose.
questions: What does it mean to have a soul that blames itself in a good way?
Why is it important to think about your purpose in life?
What do you hope to see on the Day of Resurrection?

summary: Al-Insan means 'The Human.' It says that humans were created from a mixed drop to be tested, and were shown the way, so that they could be thankful or ungrateful. It describes the righteous who feed the poor, the orphan and the captive for the sake of Allah, saying, 'We want no reward or thanks from you.' Allah rewards them with Paradise.
questions: Why do the righteous feed the poor without wanting thanks?
What is a small way you can feed or help someone this week?
What does it mean to do something purely for the sake of Allah?

summary: Al-Mursalat means 'Those Sent Forth.' It begins with oaths by the winds and repeats ten times, 'Woe on that Day to the deniers!' It reminds humans how they were created from a small drop, and how the earth holds the living and the dead. It asks, 'In what message after this will they believe?'
questions: Why do you think the same warning is repeated ten times?
How does remembering where we came from make us humble?
What message can touch your heart if the Quran does not?

summary: An-Naba means 'The Great News.' People kept asking each other about the great news, which is the Day of Judgment. Allah reminds them of His signs: the earth like a bed, mountains like pegs, sleep for rest, night like a cover, the sun like a lamp, and rain that makes gardens grow. Then it describes what is waiting for those who did wrong and for those who were mindful of Allah. It ends with the Day when a person will see what he did, and the one who denied will wish he were dust.
questions: Which sign of Allah in the first verses do you notice every day?
Why does Allah remind us of His creation before talking about the Day of Judgment?
What deed do you hope to see on the Day when you will see what you have done?

summary: An-Nazi'at means 'Those Who Pull Out.' It begins with oaths about the angels, and talks about the blast of the Trumpet. It tells the story of Musa and Pharaoh. Pharaoh said, 'I am your highest lord,' and Allah took him as a lesson for others. It reminds us of how Allah made the sky and the earth. It says the one who feared standing before his Lord and held back his soul from wrong desires will have Paradise.
questions: Why did Pharaoh's pride lead to his end?
What does it mean to hold your soul back from its desires?
What is one desire you need to control right now?

summary: Abasa means 'He Frowned.' One day a blind man, Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, came to the Prophet while he was speaking to some leaders of Quraysh. The Prophet frowned and turned away, and Allah gently corrected him, because the person who wants to learn is more important. The surah then reminds us to look at our food and how Allah made it grow, and it describes the Day when a person will run away from his own family.
questions: Why is a person who really wants to learn so valuable to Allah?
How can you make sure to treat everyone with the same respect, rich or poor?
What does it mean that on that Day a person will run from his own family?

summary: At-Takwir means 'The Folding Up.' It lists a series of signs for the Day of Judgment: the sun is folded up, the stars fall, the mountains move, the seas boil, and the girl who was buried alive is asked for what sin she was killed. Then each soul will know what it brought. The surah ends by saying the Quran is the word of a noble messenger and asks, 'So where are you going?'
questions: What does the question 'So where are you going?' make you think about?
Why do you think the surah mentions the girl who was buried alive?
How can you live today so that you are ready to know what you have brought?

summary: Al-Infitar means 'The Splitting Open.' It begins with the sky splitting and the stars scattering, and each soul knowing what it sent forward and what it left behind. Allah asks, 'O human, what has deceived you about your Generous Lord, who created you and shaped you in a balanced way?' It tells us that noble angels are writing down everything we do, and that the righteous will be in bliss.
questions: What things trick people into forgetting their Lord?
How does it change your actions to know that noble angels are writing what you do?
Why does Allah describe Himself as Generous in this surah?

summary: Al-Mutaffifin means 'Those Who Give Less.' It begins with a warning to people who cheat in weighing and measuring: when they take from others they ask for the full amount, and when they give they give less. It describes the record of the wicked and the record of the righteous. It says that those who made fun of the believers will find the believers laughing at them on that Day.
questions: Why is cheating in small things also a serious matter?
How can you be more honest in business, school or work?
How should you respond when people make fun of you for doing the right thing?

summary: Al-Inshiqaq means 'The Splitting Open.' The sky splits and the earth is stretched flat, and both obey their Lord. It says humans are working hard toward their Lord and will meet Him. The one given the record in the right hand will have an easy account and return to his people happy. The one given it behind his back will cry out for destruction. It says, 'You will surely travel from stage to stage.'
questions: What does it mean that humans are all striving toward their Lord?
How can you prepare for an easy account?
What stage of life are you in, and how can you use it well?

summary: Al-Buruj means 'The Constellations.' It tells about the people of the ditch, believers who were burned in a fire for their faith while their persecutors watched. Allah was a witness over everything. It says those who believe and do good will have gardens, and that Allah is the Forgiving and the Loving. It tells that the Quran is in a Preserved Tablet.
questions: What helped the believers in the ditch to stay firm in their faith?
What does it mean that Allah is the Loving?
How does knowing Allah sees everything comfort you?

summary: At-Tariq means 'The Night Visitor.' It says that every soul has a protector over it. It asks humans to think about what they were created from: a small drop. If Allah created them from that, He is able to bring them back. It says that on the Day, secrets will be examined. It says the Quran is a decisive word, not a joke.
questions: How can thinking about where you came from make you humble?
What secrets of the heart do you want Allah to make clean?
Why is the Quran not a joke?

summary: Al-A'la means 'The Most High.' It begins by telling us to glorify the name of our Lord, who created, shaped and guided. It reminds the Prophet that he will recite and will not forget, except what Allah wills. It says, 'Successful is the one who purifies himself, remembers the name of his Lord and prays.' It says people prefer the life of this world, but the next life is better and lasts.
questions: What does it mean to purify yourself?
Why do people prefer this world even though the next is better?
How can you remember Allah's name more during the day?

summary: Al-Ghashiyah means 'The Overwhelming.' It describes the Day of Judgment: some faces will be humbled and tired, while other faces will be happy in a high garden with flowing springs. Then it asks us to look at camels, the sky, the mountains and the earth, and to think about how they were made. It tells the Prophet that he is a reminder and not someone who can force people.
questions: What do you notice when you look carefully at the sky and the mountains?
What does it mean that the Prophet is a reminder and not a controller?
How can you remind others in a gentle way?

summary: Al-Fajr means 'The Dawn.' It begins with oaths and then reminds us of the people of Ad, Thamud and Pharaoh, who spread corruption. It says people think that wealth means Allah honors them and poverty means He disgraces them, which is wrong. It warns against not honoring the orphan, not encouraging feeding the poor and loving wealth too much. It ends with 'O soul at peace, return to your Lord, pleased and pleasing.'
questions: Does having more money mean Allah loves you more? What does the surah say?
How can you honor an orphan or someone in need?
What does it mean to have a soul at peace?

summary: Al-Balad means 'The City.' It begins with an oath by the city of Makkah. It says that humans were created in hardship, and that some boast about the wealth they spent. It reminds us that Allah gave us eyes, a tongue and lips, and showed us the two paths. The 'steep path' is freeing a slave, feeding people on a day of hunger, and being among those who encourage patience and compassion.
questions: What are the two paths Allah has shown us?
How can you help someone who is hungry or in need?
What does it mean to encourage others to patience and compassion?

summary: Ash-Shams means 'The Sun.' Allah swears by the sun, the moon, the day, the night, the sky, the earth and the soul. He says, 'Successful is the one who purifies it, and failed is the one who corrupts it.' It tells the story of Thamud, who rejected Prophet Salih and harmed the she-camel that was a sign from Allah, so they were destroyed.
questions: What does it mean to purify your soul?
What habit can help clean your heart this week?
What did the people of Thamud do that caused their destruction?

summary: Al-Layl means 'The Night.' It says that people's efforts are different. The one who gives, is mindful of Allah and believes in the best reward will find that Allah makes the way easy for him. The one who is stingy, thinks he does not need Allah and denies the best reward will find the way becomes hard for him. It says the most righteous is the one who gives to purify himself, seeking only the face of his Lord.
questions: How does giving make the way easier for a person?
Why do you think stinginess makes life harder?
How can you give today for the sake of Allah only?

summary: Ad-Duha means 'The Morning Brightness.' It was revealed to comfort the Prophet when the revelation paused for a while. Allah says, 'Your Lord has not left you, nor hated you.' It reminds him how Allah took care of him as an orphan, guided him when he was lost and gave him enough when he was poor. It tells him not to be harsh to the orphan, not to scold the one who asks, and to talk about the blessings of his Lord.
questions: How does this surah comfort someone who feels alone?
Think back: how has Allah taken care of you in the past?
How can you be kind to an orphan or someone who is asking for help?

summary: Ash-Sharh means 'The Opening.' Allah comforts the Prophet by reminding him that He opened his chest and took away his heavy burden and raised his name high. It says twice, 'Indeed, with hardship comes ease.' Then it says that when you finish one thing, you should work hard at the next, and turn your heart to your Lord.
questions: What hardship are you facing that this promise can help you with?
Why do you think Allah said 'with hardship comes ease' twice?
What can you do when you finish a task to turn toward Allah?

summary: At-Tin means 'The Fig.' Allah swears by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and the safe city of Makkah. He says that humans were created in the best form, but then they can fall to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do good deeds. It ends by asking, 'Is not Allah the most just of judges?'
questions: What does it mean that humans were created in the best form?
How can a person fall to the lowest, and how can he avoid it?
What does it mean to you that Allah is the most just of judges?

summary: Al-Alaq means 'The Clot.' The first verses of the Quran revealed to the Prophet are here, in the cave of Hira: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know.' It also warns of a man who tried to stop a servant of Allah from praying, and it ends with 'Prostrate and draw near.'
questions: Why do you think the first word revealed was 'Read'?
What new thing would you like to learn this month?
How can prostration bring a person closer to Allah?

summary: Al-Qadr means 'The Night of Power.' It says that Allah sent down the Quran on the Night of Power, and that this night is better than a thousand months. The angels and the Spirit come down in it by the permission of their Lord, and it is peace until the break of dawn. Muslims look for this night in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
questions: Why do you think one night can be better than a thousand months?
What would you do if you knew tonight was the Night of Power?
How can you make the last ten nights of Ramadan special?

summary: Al-Bayyinah means 'The Clear Proof.' It says that clear proof came to people: a messenger from Allah reading pure pages. The people who had earlier books only became divided after the clear proof came. They were only told to worship Allah sincerely, to pray and to give zakat. The ones who believe and do good are the best of creatures, and Allah is pleased with them and they with Him.
questions: What does it mean to worship Allah with sincerity?
Why is being the 'best of creatures' about belief and good deeds rather than looks or wealth?
What would it feel like for Allah to be pleased with you?

summary: Az-Zalzalah means 'The Earthquake.' On the Day of Judgment, the earth will shake with its great shaking and bring out its burdens, and people will say, 'What is wrong with it?' The earth will tell its news. Then people will be shown their deeds. 'Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.'
questions: What does it mean that even an atom's weight of good will be seen?
What small good deed can you do today that you might usually skip?
What small bad habit do you want to stop before it is counted?

summary: Al-Adiyat means 'The Charging Horses.' Allah swears by galloping war horses that rush at dawn and raise dust. Then He says that humans are very ungrateful to their Lord, and they themselves are witnesses to it, and they love wealth very much. It reminds them that when the graves are emptied and what is in the hearts is brought out, their Lord will be fully aware of them.
questions: In what ways can a person be ungrateful without noticing?
How can you check if you love wealth too much?
What do you want Allah to find in your heart on that Day?

summary: Al-Qari'ah means 'The Striking Calamity.' It is another name for the Day of Judgment. On that Day, people will be like scattered moths and the mountains will be like fluffed wool. The person whose scales are heavy with good deeds will have a happy life, but the one whose scales are light will have a deep pit of fire as his home.
questions: What can make your scale heavy with good deeds?
Why do you think people are compared to scattered moths?
What good deed can you add to your scale today?

summary: At-Takathur means 'Competing for More.' It says that competing to have more and more keeps you busy until you visit the graves. It warns, 'No! You will soon know.' It says that if you really knew with certainty, you would see the Fire with your own eyes, and then you would be asked about the blessings you enjoyed.
questions: What are things people compete to have more of today?
What blessings will you be asked about?
How can you use your blessings in a way that makes Allah pleased?

summary: Al-Asr means 'Time.' It is a very short surah. Allah swears by time that all humans are in loss, except those who believe, do good deeds, advise each other to the truth and advise each other to patience. It teaches that success needs four things: faith, good deeds, sharing the truth and being patient.
questions: Which of the four things (faith, good deeds, truth, patience) is the hardest for you?
Who is a friend who can remind you of the truth and help you be patient?
How are you using your time today?

summary: Al-Humazah means 'The Slanderer.' It warns those who talk badly about others and mock them behind their backs, and who collect wealth and keep counting it, thinking it will make them live forever. It says such a person will be thrown into the Crusher, a fire that rises up to the hearts.
questions: Why is it so harmful to talk badly about people behind their backs?
Why can wealth give a false feeling that you will live forever?
How can you use your words to help instead of to hurt?

summary: Al-Fil means 'The Elephant.' It tells about Abraha, a ruler from Yemen, who came with an army and elephants to destroy the Kaaba in the year the Prophet was born. Allah sent flocks of birds carrying small stones of baked clay, and Abraha's army became like chewed-up straw. It teaches that Allah protects His House.
questions: What does this story teach about the power of Allah compared to big armies?
How did the Kaaba stay safe even though it had no army?
When have you seen Allah protect something in a way you did not expect?

summary: Quraysh is named after the tribe of the Prophet. It reminds them of their safe trade trips in winter and summer. Because they cared for the Kaaba, people respected them and their trips were safe. So Allah tells them to worship the Lord of this House, who fed them when they were hungry and kept them safe from fear.
questions: What blessings of food and safety do you have that you can thank Allah for?
How can you show thanks to Allah with your actions?
Why should the blessing of safety and food lead us to worship Allah?

summary: Al-Ma'un means 'Small Kindnesses.' It asks, 'Have you seen the one who denies the Judgment?' It says he is the one who pushes away the orphan and does not encourage feeding the poor. Then it warns those who pray but are careless about their prayers, who show off, and who refuse even small acts of kindness.
questions: What are small kindnesses you can do for others every day?
Why does Allah connect prayer with caring for people?
How can you make your prayers more sincere, and not for show?

summary: Al-Kawthar means 'The Abundance.' It is the shortest surah in the Quran. Allah tells the Prophet that He has given him al-Kawthar, which means great abundance, and is also the name of a river in Paradise. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. It says that the one who hates him is the one cut off.
questions: What does 'abundance' mean to you?
How can you show thanks to Allah when He gives you good?
Why is it good that this surah is so short to memorize?

summary: Al-Kafirun means 'The Disbelievers.' Allah tells the Prophet to say: 'I do not worship what you worship, and you do not worship what I worship... You have your religion and I have my religion.' It teaches that a Muslim must be clear and firm that he worships Allah alone, and that he does not mix his worship with anything else, while still living peacefully with others.
questions: Why is it important to be clear about who you worship?
How can you be firm in your faith and still be kind to people who believe differently?
What does 'you have your religion and I have mine' teach about respect?

summary: An-Nasr means 'The Help.' It says that when Allah's help and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in large groups, then you should glorify your Lord with praise and ask His forgiveness, because He is the Accepter of repentance. It teaches that when we win or are successful, we should respond with thankfulness and humility.
questions: How should you act when you succeed at something?
Why does Allah tell the Prophet to ask for forgiveness at his moment of victory?
What is one success you want to thank Allah for?

summary: Al-Masad means 'The Palm Fiber.' It is about Abu Lahab, an uncle of the Prophet who harmed him and opposed his message, and his wife, who used to carry thorns. It says that his wealth and his gains did not help him. The lesson is that being related to a prophet does not save a person; faith and good deeds are what matter.
questions: Why didn't being the Prophet's relative help Abu Lahab?
What does this teach about how Allah judges people?
What should you rely on more: your family name or your deeds?

summary: Al-Ikhlas means 'Sincerity.' Allah tells the Prophet to say: 'He is Allah, the One. Allah is the Eternal, the One everyone needs. He did not have a child and was not born, and there is none equal to Him.' It is a short, clear summary of who Allah is. The Prophet said it is equal to a third of the Quran in reward.
questions: What does it mean that Allah is the One everyone needs?
How is Allah different from everything He created?
How can you remind yourself of this surah's message in daily life?

summary: Al-Falaq means 'The Daybreak.' It teaches us to seek protection with the Lord of the daybreak from the evil in what He created, from the darkness when it settles, from those who blow on knots (a kind of magic), and from the envy of an envious person. Muslims recite it, along with the next surah, in the morning, in the evening and before sleep.
questions: What does it mean to seek protection with Allah?
What can envy do to a person's heart?
How can you remember to recite this surah every morning and night?

summary: An-Nas means 'Mankind.' It is the last surah of the Quran. It teaches us to seek protection with the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind and the God of mankind, from the whisperer who hides when Allah is mentioned, who whispers into the hearts of people, from among jinn and people. It teaches that Allah is the best protector from bad thoughts.
questions: What kinds of bad thoughts or whispers come to you?
What can you do when a bad whisper comes?
Why do you think the Quran ends with a prayer for protection?
